exposure: maternal abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness (SFT) measured by ultrasonography at 18-24 weeks gestation
cohort: 158 pregnant patients attending the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at ESIC Medical College and PGIMSR, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, between January 2020 and June 2021.
finding: Maternal abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness measured at 18-24 weeks was significantly correlated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, preterm birth, cesarean section, large for gestational age, NICU admissions, and low APGAR score.
mod_finding: Increased maternal subcutaneous fat thickness was significantly correlated with an increased risk of cesarean section.
birth_weight: N/A (measured as an outcome, no specific range for inclusion)
gest_age: N/A (measured as an outcome, no specific range for inclusion)
